previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after awakening with severe substernal chest pain radiating to her back, diagnosed with a Type A aortic dissection involving the ascending and descending aorta. She underwent emergent ascending aortic and hemiarch graft replacement, followed by reoperation for postoperative bleeding with temporary chest closure. She experienced complications including heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, bilateral upper extremity deep vein thromboses, postoperative atrial fibrillation requiring cardioversion, and acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with pulmonary edema requiring aggressive diuresis and ventilator support. A urinary tract infection was treated with oral ciprofloxacin, and a new left knee effusion was evaluated but found not to be septic. She was successfully weaned off the ventilator by postoperative day 9, transitioned to oral intake, and transferred to a step-down unit. By discharge, she was ambulating steadily, alert, and managing pain with oral medications. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with a plan for outpatient MRA of the aorta with premedication for contrast allergy.

# Acute on Chronic Diastolic Heart Failure: The history was 
difficult to interpret because it was unclear whether she has 
orthopnea as she reports sleeping on less pillows. However, her 
weight gain (patient reports that her dry weight is 
approximately 135lbs) and dyspnea on exertion do support the 
diagnosis of acute chronic diastolic heart failure (last EF 
50-55% in ___ with the inciting factors being medication 
non-compliance after having stopped her bumex whent he 
prescription ran out and dietary indiscretions. The diagnosis of 
a pulmonary embolus was considered and elevated D-dimer to 7900 
was concerning. However, with her iodine allergy causing 
hypotension, CTA could not be performed. With her history of 
possible HIT it was determined not to empirically anticoagulate 
because the risks of anticoagulation outweighed the benefits as 
she was hemodynamically stable. V/Q scan and LENIs were negative 
making pulmonary embolus unlikely. The patient was diuresed 
using lasix 40mg IV daily. She was approximately 4L net negative 
during her hospitalization and she was discharged with a weight 
of 61.8kg. She was restarted on her home dose of furosemide 40mg 
daily.
